Thank you all three for bringing these constraints forward — they're all directly relevant to the decisions I need to finalize. Let me summarize what I'm hearing so I can make sure I've got it right before I settle:

1. Theo: The legacy pipeline has a prepaid capacity commitment running through January 31, 2026. Retiring before that strands committed capacity — so there's a financial constraint pointing toward a retirement date on or after that date.

2. Rina: Compliance requires production audit events to be stored in immutable storage for exactly 365 days and must bypass sampling entirely. This needs to be reflected in the transition settings and follow-up work.

3. Owen: The legacy_exporter service can't switch readers atomically and requires exactly 14 days of dual-write coverage before the old pipeline reader can be safely disabled. This means the retirement date needs to be at least 14 days after we start the dual-write period.

So the way I see it, the earliest sensible retirement date would be at least 14 days after we begin dual-writing, and it should also align with or come after January 31, 2026 to avoid stranding the capacity commitment. The transition settings need to include the 14-day dual-write window, immutable 365-day audit retention, and no sampling on audit events.

Before I finalize, I want to make sure all three of these get formally captured. Theo, can you update the change ticket with the capacity commitment information? Rina, can you file the compliance note against the migration? And Owen, can you get your local migration note into the ticketing system as well? Once those are recorded, I'll settle the production plan.
